solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Some idle drunk to play music

indicators.note: someone drunk staggers about, so the letters of these two words are jumbled up

explanation.surface: A bit of idle drinking leads someone to start making music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' scrambles SOME and IDLE together. 'Some' looks like 'a portion of', which tempts a hidden-word hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: To melodise is to compose or perform a tune, making melodies, which is playing music.

clue.text: Old vehicle beginning to rust in pit

parts.note: a crate is slang for an old, battered car

indicators.note: the opening letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: An abandoned old car rusts away at the bottom of a pit.
explanation.walkthrough: CRATE is informal for a clapped-out car; add R, the start of 'rust'.
explanation.definitionFit: A crater is a bowl-shaped hollow in the ground, a kind of pit.

clue.text: Strange deities, about a thousand, put into list

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the next piece, enclosing it
something strange is out of its normal form, so the letters of deities are rearranged

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Someone catalogues a thousand odd gods in a long inventory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' rearranges DEITIES, and 'about' wraps those letters round M.
explanation.definitionFit: To itemise is to set out item by item, so itemised describes things entered on a list.

clue.text: Like something wicked making one irritable?

definitions.meaning: a candle has a wick, and is made of wax, so wax-like means like a wicked thing, wicked read as having a wick
bad-tempered; in British slang to be in a wax is to be in a temper

explanation.surface: Something evil puts a person in a foul temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wicked' here means having a wick, like a candle, not evil. Being 'in a wax' is old British slang for being angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Candles are made of wax and carry wicks; separately, waxy is British slang for cross or bad-tempered.

clue.text: Put an end to game

definitions.meaning: to stop or crush something, such as a rebellion or a rumour
a racket sport played against the walls of an enclosed court

explanation.surface: Someone calls a halt to a match.
explanation.definitionFit: To squash a plan is to suppress it; squash is also an indoor racket sport.

clue.text: Appearance of soldiers capturing island

indicators.note: one piece takes the other prisoner, holding it inside

parts.note: men is a common word for soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: A description of how troops look as they seize an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Mien is a person's look or bearing, their outward manner and expression.

clue.text: Taunt from joker, no good person at heart

indicators.note: no says the following piece is missing from the word before it
the missing piece is taken from the middle of the word for joker

parts.note: a jester is a court joker or fool
ST is the abbreviation for saint, a good person

explanation.surface: A clown who is a bad person inside mocks people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' and 'at heart' together remove ST, a saint, from the middle of JESTER. 'no good' looks like a phrase, but 'good person' belongs together.
explanation.definitionFit: To jeer is to mock or scoff at someone, which is what a taunt does.

clue.text: Cool-headed way in which Greek character protects queen

indicators.note: the following pieces sit inside the word for way

parts.note: a trail is a path or way

indicators.note: the Greek letter surrounds the queen, shielding her

parts.note: nu is the thirteenth letter of the Greek alphabet
Q is the abbreviation for queen, as in chess notation

explanation.surface: A calm route on which a Greek guards a queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protects' wraps the Greek letter round Q, and 'in which' sets that group inside the way. 'Greek character' suggests a person, but it is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A tranquil person is calm and unruffled, which is what being cool-headed means.

clue.text: Weaver as lowest of the low?

definitions.meaning: Nick ... is the weaver in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream
the very lowest part or position of anything

explanation.surface: A weaver seen as the humblest person there is.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottom is the weaver given an ass's head in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: The weaver in Shakespeare's comedy bears this name; the word also means the lowest point.

clue.text: Longs to have time with partners at table

parts.note: a year is a period of time
North and South are partners at the bridge table, N and S

explanation.surface: Someone wants time with fellow players at a card table.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North and South play as partners against East and West.
explanation.definitionFit: To yearn is to long or pine for something with intense desire.

clue.text: Row right after cup game?

indicators.note: the abbreviation for right comes after the cup game in the answer

parts.note: in British football a cup match is called a cup tie

explanation.surface: An argument breaks out straight after a cup match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a quarrel, which suits a football crowd, but it is a line of seats. A TIE is a knockout cup match in British sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is one of a series of rows placed one above another, as in stadium seating.

clue.text: Big horse eats a medium soft plant

indicators.note: the horse takes the next pieces inside it, as if swallowing them

parts.note: a shire is a large heavy draught horse
M is the abbreviation for medium, as in clothing sizes
P stands for piano, soft in music

explanation.surface: A large horse munches on a moderately soft plant.
explanation.walkthrough: A SHIRE horse is a big British breed of draught horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Samphire is a fleshy coastal plant that grows on cliffs and salt marshes, eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Communications taking long time after disorder

indicators.note: the word for a long period comes after the word for disorder in the answer

parts.note: a mess is a state of untidiness or confusion
ages means a very long time, as in waiting for ages

explanation.surface: Messages are slow to arrive after an upheaval.
explanation.definitionFit: Messages are things sent from one person to another, which is what communications are.

clue.text: Minor act excited one sort of poet

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up, so those of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A small, overwrought performance stirs up a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Keats, Shelley and Byron belong to the Romantic movement, a school of poets.

clue.text: Chemical compounds got from crumbling deep pits

indicators.note: crumbling things fall apart, so the letters of the two words break up and re-form

explanation.surface: Minerals extracted from collapsing deep mines.
explanation.definitionFit: Peptides are short chains of amino acids, compounds studied in biochemistry.

clue.text: Awkward time with Richard

parts.note: Ricky is a familiar short form of the name Richard

explanation.surface: Spending time with a man called Richard is uncomfortable.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricky situation is difficult to handle, hence awkward.

clue.text: A female making comeback, this person is celebrity

indicators.note: coming back means the two letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the setter referring to themselves as this person gives me

explanation.surface: A woman returning to the stage is now a star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making comeback' turns A plus F round to make FA. 'this person' means the setter, ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Fame and celebrity both mean the state of being widely known and talked about.

clue.text: Encourage replanting of forest

indicators.note: replanting puts the trees in new places, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A call to support the replanting of woodland.
explanation.definitionFit: To foster growth or talent is to nurture and promote it.

clue.text: Foreign minister — namely, one to accompany Her Majesty

parts.note: viz is the abbreviation for videlicet, Latin for namely
I is the Roman numeral for one
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen

explanation.surface: An overseas official arrives with an escort for the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreign minister' suggests a country's diplomat, but here it means a minister from abroad. ER is Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: A vizier was a high official or minister in Muslim states such as the Ottoman Empire.

clue.text: Monk initially entering an hour after midnight as man of prayer

indicators.note: the letter goes into the time, inside it

parts.note: one o'clock in the morning is 1 AM, with the figure written as I

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A monk comes in at one in the morning to pray.
explanation.walkthrough: The time is written as 1 AM, with the figure 1 read as the letter I; 'initially' and 'entering' put the monk's first letter inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An imam leads the prayers in a mosque, so he is a man of prayer.

clue.text: Engineers at home making check

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: Engineers in their house carry out an inspection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'check' is the noun meaning a restraint, not an inspection.
explanation.definitionFit: A rein is a restraint, as in keeping a rein on spending, so it is a check.

clue.text: Sailor dispatched, not here

parts.note: AB is an able seaman, an ordinary sailor
sent means dispatched, sent off

explanation.surface: A sailor has been sent away, so is missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone absent is away or missing, so they are not present.

clue.text: Support team that is 9

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: Supporting the team, which is what 9 says.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to the answer at 9 across, BOTTOM, in its sense of the body's rear.
explanation.definitionFit: Backside and bottom are both everyday words for the buttocks.

clue.text: Wickedness not recorded after revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns the word round, so it is read backwards

parts.note: a live broadcast is not recorded beforehand

explanation.surface: Evil deeds after an uprising go undocumented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after revolution' turns LIVE back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Evil is moral badness, the same as wickedness.
